Read-only: do not edit files.

entry.text:
Q1: src/hub.ts:65 `static DEFAULT_NUDGE_MS = Number(process.env.CHATROOM_NUDGE_AFTER_MS ?? 180_000)`; applied per room hub.ts:94; legacy fallback src/hub/persistence.ts:77.
 Effect sites: (a) silence nudge hub.ts:1036-1058, re-armed by every post() at hub.ts:985 (incl. its own system post), identical nudge posted at most twice (1054-1056). (b) openings deadline: armed at 2 periods on creation (hub.ts:136), re-armed to 1 period by first opening (1081), unarrived seats get one warning + one more period (1101-1105), then reveal (1107). (c) user-visible minute text: server.ts:325-328, 442, 464.
 Verdict: keep 3 min. In a 9-seat room any post resets (a), so it only fires on true room-wide silence and is self-limiting; lengthening it would mostly delay (b), where one straggler of nine would otherwise hold eight seats. Shortening risks nudges/reveals while seats are mid tool work (reading code, running tests takes minutes).
Q2: grep -oE "'[^']+\.(ts|mjs|js)'" | sort | uniq -c → bench-build-oracle-audit.test.ts at offline-runner.mjs:64 and :78 is the only repeat inside offlineScripts (lines 26-182). seat-env-regression.ts / claude-lean-flags-regression.ts also count 2 but their 2nd occurrence is the --experimental-vm-modules condition at :192, NOT the list.
Q3: src/server.ts:21 `MAX_WAIT_MS = 55_000; // stay under typical MCP client tool timeouts (Codex 60s)`; enforced by zod max at :348 and Math.min at :359. Justified: 5s margin under 60s; DEFAULT_WAIT_MS (:20) equals it, and hold_until_actionable re-polls server-side within the same waitDeadline (:360-362), so longer effective holds don't need a larger cap.

proposal.text:
Q1 (judgement): KEEP the 3-minute default. Set at src/hub.ts:65 (`DEFAULT_NUDGE_MS = Number(process.env.CHATROOM_NUDGE_AFTER_MS ?? 180_000)`), applied per room at hub.ts:94. Where it takes effect: (a) the silence nudge, hub.ts:1036-1058, which every post() re-arms (hub.ts:985) and which posts the same text at most twice (1054-1056), so with nine seats it fires only on real room-wide silence and stops itself; (b) the blind-openings deadline: two periods from room creation (hub.ts:136), one period from the first opening (1081), one warning plus one more period for seats that never joined (1101-1105), then reveal (1107). That keeps eight seats from waiting long on one straggler. Making it longer would mainly slow (b). Making it shorter risks nudges and early reveals while seats are still reading code or running tests. The minute values are also shown to users at server.ts:325-328, 442 and 464.
Q2: Only bench-build-oracle-audit.test.ts appears twice in the explicit offlineScripts list (scripts/offline-runner.mjs:64 and :78). seat-env-regression.ts and claude-lean-flags-regression.ts each show up a second time only in the --experimental-vm-modules condition at :192, which is outside the list.
Q3 (judgement): MAX_WAIT_MS = 55_000 at src/server.ts:21, with the comment "stay under typical MCP client tool timeouts (Codex 60s)". It is enforced at :348 (zod max) and :359 (Math.min). The cap is still justified: it leaves a 5s margin under the 60s client timeout. wait() returns as soon as an event arrives, so the cap adds no latency, and hold_until_actionable re-polls on the server inside the same deadline (:360-362), so longer effective holds do not need a larger cap.
